resources.string: Closing a session drops its transcript from view. It cannot kill anything still executing inside Termux — a background RUN_COMMAND returns no live process handle to signal.
Long-press a session to rename it.

A session here is a named run-group over the one-shot RUN_COMMAND contract, not a live interactive PTY. A failsafe session dispatches under bash --norc --noprofile so a broken startup file cannot lock you out. A real interactive terminal needs an NDK build; every native tree in this repository is empty.
Extra-keys toolbar needs a live terminal view

ESC / CTRL / TAB / arrow keys act on a live terminal view, which this build does not host — commands are dispatched one-shot in the background, with no key stream to feed. The text-insert row below is backable and enabled; the modifier keys are not.
Click a URL to copy it
No URL found in the transcript.
Trim to the text you want, then share
Terminal appearance (font, cursor, colours) lives under Settings ▸ Terminal & Editor and is not wired to this surface, so Style is inert here rather than a control that changes nothing.
Terminal settings live under Settings ▸ Terminal & Editor; no route reaches them from the Shell screen yet, so this opens nothing rather than pretending to.
Killing a process needs a live pid, which the one-shot background RUN_COMMAND never returns. There is no pid to signal from here.
Autofill targets a live terminal view\'s input field. This build hosts no such view, so there is nothing to fill.
No jobs yet. Each command you run becomes a background job here, so a long command never freezes the composer.
Stopping a background RUN_COMMAND is not cleanly cancellable over the one-shot contract; the job keeps running inside Termux. Dismiss only stops tracking it here.
Each row is `command -v X && X --version` over the installed Termux. An absent tool reports not detected — the readout cannot claim what is not there.
Backed by pkg/apt inside Termux: list-installed, du -sh, install, upgrade, uninstall.
No installed packages parsed. Refresh, or the list is empty.
proot · system shell · storage permissions · distro · network · abnormalities — each a scripted probe, each reporting whatever it actually found.
Read from proot-distro list. Install, upgrade, reset and uninstall are destructive rootfs operations held in reserve and not wired to a live control here.
proot-distro is not installed inside Termux, so there is no rootfs list to read. Install it from Packages first.

Scripts under ~/.termux/boot. Listing, editing, enabling and running them is backed by RUN_COMMAND file ops. Boot-time execution itself depends on the separate Termux:Boot app, which this build has no way to detect (no queries entry for it) — treat enablement as a filesystem fact, not a guarantee it runs at boot.
The ~/.termux/boot directory does not exist yet. Creating a boot task will make it.

Backup tars ~ into a timestamped archive under HOME (backable). Restore reads an archive from a Storage Access Framework tree, which needs a content-URI stream into Termux that the one-shot contract cannot cleanly provide — it is gated. Expose over SAF opens a folder picker so another app can reach a chosen tree.

Restoring means streaming an archive from a SAF content URI into Termux\'s filesystem. The background RUN_COMMAND contract has no clean way to pipe that content in, so restore is inert here rather than a control that silently drops your data.
